$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: One note per CSF 2.0 subcategory from the 'CSF 2.0' sheet of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 reference workbook — 185 subcategory rows, of which 106 are current outcomes and 79 are withdrawal markers retained from CSF v1.1. The sheet's real header row is row 2; row 1 is a banner. PROPERTIES: subcategory_id (the identity, e.g. 'GV.OC-01'), plus function (6 values) and category (34 values) DERIVED from that identifier by splitting on '.' and '-'. Those two are short, closed, enumerable facets — exactly what Bases groups by and what the Tier 2 projection indexes. They are derived rather than read from the sheet's own Function and Category columns because that sheet is a merged-cell banner layout: those columns carry text only on their own function/category rows and are empty on every subcategory row (verified across all 185 rows; every id matches XX.YY-NN, so the two splits are total). curie is emitted automatically from source.ontology plus the identifier and is deliberately not declared here. BODY: the Subcategory cell verbatim as an '## Outcome' section, and the Implementation Examples cell as an '## Implementation examples' bulleted list — the workbook packs 1 to 10 examples into a single cell separated by newlines, and format 'list' bullets each non-empty line, so 'Ex1: …', 'Ex2: …' arrive as list items. omit_if_empty (the default) keeps that section off the 79 withdrawn subcategories, which have no examples. PROPERTIES-VS-BODY RATIONALE: this revision is the whole point of the change — the previous recipe emitted subcategory_id and a title and nothing else, so every generated note had a zero-word body and the framework's actual content was discarded on import. A CSF subcategory has no short name the way an 800-53 control does: its 'title' IS its outcome statement (33 to 208 characters, median 101). Projected as frontmatter that puts a full sentence in Obsidian's property panel, where it is truncated, awkward to escape in YAML, and invisible to body search; in the body it is readable and searchable. The title property is therefore dropped, not duplicated. No H1 is emitted: the note's filename already carries the identifier and Obsidian renders it, so a heading repeating it is noise. RIGHTS: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 is a public-domain United States Government work. The workbook is tracked in the corpus, so the recipe, sample output, and screenshots of generated content may all be committed. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. KNOWN GAP 1 — Informative References is emitted nowhere, deliberately. It is a cross-framework mapping column: each cell packs newline-separated '<framework label>: <identifier>' pairs across six different target frameworks (CCM v4.0, CRI Profile v2.0, CSF v1.1, SP 800-218, SP 800-221A, SP 800-53 Rev 5.1.1). Turning it into resolvable wikilinks or CURIEs needs a per-item split-and-map the closed grammar does not have: template filters operate on one scalar and cannot map over list items, managed_links can split and wrap each piece in [[…]] but cannot strip the framework label from each piece, and body projections cannot expand a list into per-item links. The honest output today would be [[CCMv4.0: BCR-01]], which is worse than nothing. These are mapping assertions between two ontologies and belong in a crosswalk / mapping-set import (see recipes/import/crosswalks), not flattened onto the concept note. KNOWN GAP 2 — the grammar cannot express 'everything after the first colon', which is why the outcome statement is projected verbatim, identifier prefix included, rather than split. split(:,1) returns only the second colon-delimited piece, and 79 of the 185 rows are withdrawal markers carrying a second colon ('ID.AM-06: [Withdrawn: Incorporated into GV.RR-02, GV.SC-02]'), so split(:,1) silently truncates them to '[Withdrawn' and loses the incorporation target — the only content a withdrawn subcategory has. The previous recipe shipped exactly that truncation in its title property. regex() cannot rescue it: its argument may not contain ')' (src/render/template.ts:247, the filter-argument pattern is [^)]*), so a capture group is impossible, and '|' is reserved by the template parser, so there is no alternation (src/render/template.ts:222). ROW SELECTION (SchemaVer 1.9.0 — this replaces what was KNOWN GAP 3, which said no row predicate existed) — the sheet interleaves 12 function banner rows and 34 category banner rows with the 185 subcategory rows, and on a banner row the Subcategory cell is empty, so before a row predicate existed all 46 banners rendered an empty file template and collided on the filename '.md'. source.where is "Subcategory != ''", which admits exactly the 185 subcategory rows and excludes exactly the 46 banners. Verified against the shipped export: the 'CSF 2.0' sheet (real header on row 2) yields 231 data rows, 185 with a non-empty Subcategory and 46 strictly empty, none whitespace-only, so no $trim is needed here. This recipe can now be pointed at the whole sheet; no pre-filtered row selection is required. The predicate runs before identity, CURIE minting, concept_cid and render(), so an excluded banner mints no CURIE and cannot surface as an orphan on re-import, and a mistyped column name is refused at preflight (naming the available columns) rather than silently admitting zero rows.
